Subject: Notification of Authorised Officers and Officers competent to levy and recover damages
under Chapter II of the Code on Social Security, 2020 — Initiation and conduct of proceedings
under Sections 125 and 128 thereof — reg.

Madan//Sir,

Enclosed please find herewith a copy of the Gazette notification no- 2695 (E)and 2699 (E) dated
29th May, 2026, conferring powers upon the Officers of the EPFO to function as Authorised Officers and
Officers competent to levy and recover damages for the purposes of Chapter III of the Code on Social
Security, 2020.

However, for smooth implementation of the above, following administrative and jurisdictional
guidelines are issued in supersession of all earlier instructions issued in this regard for the conduct of

proceedings under Sections 125 and 128 of the Code.

The Competent Authority has directed that, notwithstanding the notification conferring all-India
Jurisdiction upon Authorised Officers and Officers competent to levy and recover damages, such
jurisdiction shall be exercised by the officers posted at respective Regional/District office in accordance
with the jurisdictional allocation as appended below.

# Bigger Regional Offices are such offices, which have more than 200 total number of establishment under
its jurisdiction with more than 1000 employees at the time of closure of the last financial year.

*Smaller Regional Offices are such offices, which have less than 200 total number of establishments under
its jurisdiction with more than 1000 employees at the time of closure of the last financial year.

The subscriber strength for the purpose of allocating proceedings shall be determined by the
number of contributory UANs in the Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR) filed for the one month prior
to the first month of the default period in respect of which the proceeding is proposed to be initiated. For
instance, in case, proceeding is proposed to be initiated for the period April 2022 to February 2025, the
number of contributory UANs in the establishment in March 2022 shall be the basis of determination of
jurisdiction. However, in case such information is not available on record due to any reason whatsoever,
the jurisdiction shall be on the basis of information relating to number of contributory UANs, last available

on record.

It is however, clarified that once a proceeding is initiated by the jurisdictional officer, any
subsequent fluctuation in contributory UAN strength during the proceedings shall not result in transfer of
the case to an officer of a different level.

Further, in offices where an Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner is not posted, the functions
and responsibilities of the Authorised Officer shall be discharged by the Regional Provident Fund

Commissioner-II.

It is also directed that although Enforcement Officer has been notified as ‘Officer authorized to
levy and recover damages under section 128 of the Code’ through the aforesaid notification, such powers
shall be exercised only by senior-level Enforcement Officers drawing pay in the pre-revised Grade Pay of
%5,400/- or its equivalent level in the prevailing Pay Matrix. In such offices, where no Enforcement Officer
is posted in the specified grade pay, the responsibility shall be assigned to the APFC/RPFC-II as the case
may be.

Should a shortage of officers or other compelling administrative reason make the prescribed
allocation impracticable, the Regional PF Commissioner-in-charge (OIC) may forward a self-contained
proposal to the Additional CPFC (Zone) for consideration. The ACC (Zone) shall be competent to decide
on such proposals for deviation and decision of the ACC (Zone) on such proposal shall be conveyed within
three days of its receipt, under intimation to the Head Office.

Cases remanded by various Courts/Tribunals for rehearing under sections 125 or 128 shall be
assigned for hearing to the officer specified in the matrix below:

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 29th May, 2026 
 
S.O. 2695(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (5) of section 2 of the Code on Social Security, 
2020 (36 of 2020),  the Central Government hereby authorises the Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Additional 
Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner and Assistant Provident Fund 
Commissioner, to function as  authorised officers for the purposes of Chapter III of the said Code.
